answer: DOWNREGULATION is the direction that primarily drives the CBD effect in the primary (CBD-vs-vehicle) comparison — on the differential-expression evidence. I ran the full limma-voom pipeline (Python: TMM → log2CPM → voom mean–variance weights → eBayes moderation → BH) on the primary contrast CBD_IC50 (g7) vs DMSO (g3, its vehicle, full serum): 6,925 downregulated vs 570 upregulated genes at padj<0.05 & |log2FC|>0.5 (7,495 total). This is robust to the significance threshold: 68% of all 27,494 tested genes trend down and the median log2FC is −0.119, so the CBD transcriptomic response is overwhelmingly a downregulatory program. The two sensitivity contrasts flip only weakly (g8v4: 3,986 up vs 2,590 down, median log2FC +0.043; g9v5: 2,803 up vs 2,146 down, median +0.023), i.e. near-neutral, so the primary CBD-vs-vehicle signal is the dominant one and it is down-dominated. CAVEAT ON THE METABOLIC CALL: the required GO-Biological-Process enrichment — the step that would confirm the downregulated set is enriched for metabolic processes — could NOT be executed in this environment. I probed the provisioned environment: no Ensembl-keyed human GO-BP annotation (org.Hs.eg.db / GOA / BP GMT), no R/clusterProfiler, network blocked, and no symbol<->Ensembl map present. Per your protocol I did NOT fabricate gene→GO mappings, so the "metabolic" confirmation is pending. The directional call (downregulation) therefore rests on the DEA, not on the enrichment; feeding an Ensembl-keyed BP annotation (or a symbol<->Ensembl map + network/R) is all that's needed to close the loop and confirm the metabolic BP terms.
